payload.claim: The spec declares risk: standard, but its touches list includes saffron/ledger.py, which is listed verbatim in .saffron/policy.yaml's elevate_on. saffron/repos/policy.py::effective_risk computes elevated whenever any changed file matches an elevate_on pattern, computed from the actual diff rather than from touches or the spec's declared risk. So this task will run at effective risk elevated regardless of what the frontmatter says, which makes the size gate blocking rather than advisory and marks the queue entry for a person to read cold rather than skim (DESIGN.md §5.6). This is very likely harmless here: the production diff is small (~20 lines, well under the 1300-token bug ceiling) and the new/expanded test files sit under the declared test_paths: ["tests/**"], so size_gate excludes their tokens from the count entirely (SA-0274). But the declared risk: standard is simply not the tier this attempt will actually run under, and a person approving this spec before it is built should know that up front.
